entry.evidence: The expected geological section is based on the interpretation of the geophysical site investigations, which are detailed in Juhlin et al. (2016).

steps.action: Set the scientific targets of COSC-2, including the nature of the main décollement and the origin of the deep basement reflectors.
steps.quote: The origin and nature of the prominent, deep basement reflectors imaged in the seismic profiles

steps.action: Stated the expected section from the group's site investigations: décollement at the 1200–1250 m reflection in Alum Shale, MT-predicted Alum Shale at ca. 750 m above an imbricate system, and Rätan granite basement inferred from magnetic data (Dyrelius 1980).
steps.quote: It was interpreted as being the detachment between the Lower Allochthon and the autochthonous basement, i.e. the main Caledonian décollement.

steps.action: Listed rival interpretations of the 1.5–2.0 km basement reflections: major fault zones, dolerite intrusions, or both.
steps.quote: which were interpreted to either be (1) major fault zones of yet unknown, but possibly Caledonian age, (2) dolerite intrusions

steps.action: Designed the borehole to penetrate the predicted units and fixed a stopping criterion tied to the basement reflections.
steps.quote: Drilling would stop, and the borehole would be completed once the nature of the basement rocks beneath these reflections was established.

steps.action: Drilled and fully cored COSC-2A to 2276 m and COSC-2B to 116 m (HQ3, NQ3, then NQ double tube), with core recovery close to 100 %.
steps.quote: The drilling operations aimed at full-core coverage from the surface to total depth.

steps.action: Established an on-site protocol for contamination-free microbiological core sampling: washing, flame sterilisation, inner-core sampling and preservation.
steps.quote: The surface of the core was flamed to combust contaminating nucleic acids from microbes present in the drilling fluid.

steps.action: Checked decontamination with fluorescent microsphere tracers in the drilling fluid, and sampled the drilling fluid to identify contaminant taxa.
steps.quote: [...] success of surface decontamination, fluorescent microspheres (AFN-09, Radiant Color NV) 0.25–0.45 µ m in diameter were added to the drilling fluid

steps.action: Microspheres adhered to clay in the drilling fluid, so below 700 m the tracer was applied by submersing the retrieved core.
steps.quote: Due to the adhesion of the fluorescent microspheres to the clay particles in the drilling fluid, the beads were no longer added

steps.action: Used the new mDIS drilling information system for on-site data acquisition and reported it ready for production workflows.
steps.quote: COSC-2 could demonstrate that this software is ready for production workflows after 2 years of development

steps.action: Described the core lithologies (greywackes, sheared black shale at ca. 780 m, sandstones and conglomerates, porphyries from 1250 m, dolerites at 1600–1930 m) and logged the boreholes with a full downhole suite.
steps.quote: the borehole encountered a strongly sheared black shale unit, which is in accordance with the magnetotelluric site investigations

steps.action: Built a common depth reference by correlating logs to a master gamma log and matching unrolled core scans to acoustic televiewer images in Corelyzer.
steps.quote: the depth of the unrolled core scans was adjusted until these images matched the structures observed in the acoustic televiewer imagery

steps.action: Compared the borehole path from the north-seeking gyro with the televiewer accelerometer/magnetometer orientation.
steps.quote: The gyro and televiewer orientation match closely (Fig. 5) but with a slightly higher deviation of the Abi43.

steps.action: Compared the expected geological section with the drilled section on the depth-converted seismic image.
steps.quote: Comparing the expected geological section with the drilled section (Fig. 2) allows a number of observations.

steps.action: Rejected the imbricate-system interpretation: the Alum Shale lies in its original stratigraphic position, and Rätan-type granite was not encountered.
steps.quote: This ca. 45 m thick unit at ∼ 800 m is the Alum Shale Formation in its original stratigraphic position.

steps.action: Kept dolerite intrusions, with some marginal deformation, as the source of the 1.5–2 km basement reflections.
steps.quote: the prominent reflections between ∼ 1.5 and 2 km correspond, as expected, to dolerites

steps.action: Revised the section: décollement in the Alum Shale at 780–825 m, a thickened sedimentary cover, the 1250 m reflection at the top of the Dala Porphyries, and Rätan granite deeper.
steps.quote: the main detachment horizon that occurs a level of ca. 780–825 m, instead of the expected depth of ca. 1250 m

steps.action: Computed a preliminary synthetic seismogram from the P-wave sonic log (constant density, Gaussian-derivative wavelet, 80 Hz).
steps.quote: The P-wave sonic log (Fig. 6) was used as input for generating a preliminary synthetic seismogram that can be compared with the surface seismic data.

steps.action: Compared the synthetic seismogram with the surface seismic section: Alum Shale, porphyry top and dolerite contacts match reflections.
steps.quote: Good correlation is observed between the synthetic seismogram and the surface data (Fig. 7).

steps.action: Reported the disturbed borehole temperature profile and thermal gradient, which await thermal equilibration.
steps.quote: requires that the borehole temperature (Fig. 8) equilibrates to a steady state after the disturbance by the drilling operations

steps.action: Concluded that the target of understanding the basement seismic reflectivity was addressed, with further seismic work to follow.
steps.quote: the project successfully addressed the target of understanding the seismic reflectivity in the basement

end.claim: The drilled section contradicts the site-investigation interpretation: the main Caledonian décollement lies in the Alum Shale at ca. 780–825 m, not at the 1250 m reflection, which marks the top of the Dala Porphyries, while the 1.5–2 km basement reflections correspond to dolerites.

decisive_move.sentence: Recovering a continuous core that showed sheared Alum Shale at ca. 780 m and porphyries from 1250 m is what overturned the expected section.

gates.evidence: The expected section and the reflector rivals were published before drilling (Juhlin et al. 2016; Yan et al. 2016) and fixed the site and the stopping criterion (§2 ¶1, §2.2 ¶1). That expectation faced a test it failed. The revised décollement position is asserted from core observations ('we regard it'), checked only by a preliminary synthetic seismogram correlation (§5 ¶3).

limits: The paper is a preliminary science report; no review file was supplied, so the review sequence is not coded. The revised décollement position rests on core observation without strain or microstructural data, which the paper postpones. The synthetic seismogram assumes constant density, uses a single trace, and is stated to need improved time/depth conversion. No uncertainties are given. Sub-claims at other statuses: drilling, core recovery and the common depth/orientation reference system are capability_characterized; the microbiological sampling protocol is claimed viable (capability_characterized), but the tracer results are not reported and laboratory validation is pending; the dolerite origin of the reflections, the thickened sedimentary cover and the deeper Rätan granite are best_explanation (the granite position is an inference with no direct test). Composition is none_fits: the walk resembles forecast_verification (an expectation fixed before drilling, observation later), but the expectation was an interpretive section, not a computed forecast, and it was not scored against a reference. A single borehole gives no repetition, so trace_series does not fit either. The heat-flow, hydrogeology, palaeoenvironment and microbiology targets have no results yet. Coding the entry as hypothesis is an inference from the framing of §2.2.

disagreements.target: Site-investigation interpretation (Juhlin et al., 2016): main décollement at the 1200–1250 m reflection with an imbricate Alum Shale system above
disagreements.support: The core shows Alum Shale in its original stratigraphic position at ca. 780–825 m and porphyry basement from 1250 m; the synthetic seismogram ties the 1250 m reflection to the porphyry top.
disagreements.quote: this shale was not transported upwards from the décollement at about 1250 m in an imbricate system, as interpreted [...]

disagreements.target: Former interpretations of the Rätan granite extending beneath the COSC area (Dyrelius, 1980)
disagreements.support: Rätan-type granite was not encountered; the basement is weakly magnetic Dala Porphyry to at least 2.3 km.
disagreements.quote: In contrast to former interpretations, the Rätan-type granite that is responsible for the regional magnetic anomaly is now expected to be located at greater depth.

disagreements.target: Sedimentary basement cover usually only some tens of metres thick along the Caledonian front (Andersson et al., 1985; Juhlin et al., 2016)
disagreements.support: The borehole shows ca. 425 m (825–1250 m) of coarse siliciclastics in turbiditic background sediments between the Alum Shale and the basement.
disagreements.quote: appears to be substantially thicker than observed at the nearest basement window
